skill.name: claude-code-hooks
skill.description: Learn how to configure Claude Code hooks for validation, audit logging, approvals, and session automation.
skill.summary: Configure Claude Code hooks to run scripts before and after tool events.
skill.author: 0xDarkMatter

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples that document Claude Code hook configuration, shell snippets, and safety deny-lists. The main confirmed issue is that two audit logging examples persist full or raw tool input, which can expose secrets or sensitive project data in logs.

remediation.issue: Audit examples log full hook input or raw tool_input fields.
remediation.suggestion: Replace these examples with allow-listed fields and redact secrets, file contents, prompt text, and command arguments before writing logs.

remediation.issue: Secret-loading examples may normalize broad environment access in hooks.
remediation.suggestion: Add a warning to load only required variables and never echo, log, or forward environment values from hook scripts.

remediation.issue: Examples rely on user-authored shell scripts for enforcement.
remediation.suggestion: Emphasize quoting, JSON validation, timeouts, and project-scoped paths in every copyable hook template.

static_findings.snippet: **See Also:** `claude-code-debug` for troubleshooting, `claude-code-headless` for CLI automation

semantic_findings.title: Audit Logging Can Capture Sensitive Tool Input
semantic_findings.description: The documentation includes audit log examples that write full hook input or raw tool_input fields to local logs. Tool input may include prompts, commands, file paths, file contents, or credentials, so examples should demonstrate sanitization by default.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both cited examples directly append unsanitized hook input data to audit logs. The security-patterns file warns about full input logging elsewhere, but the audit examples still show potentially sensitive fields being persisted.

content.value_statement: Claude Code hooks are powerful, but unsafe hook scripts can leak data or block work unexpectedly. This skill explains hook events, configuration patterns, and safer script templates for controlled automation.
actual_capabilities: Explains Claude Code hook events and when each event runs.
Shows settings.json patterns for PreToolUse, PostToolUse, and SessionStart hooks.
Provides shell examples for parsing hook JSON input with jq.
Documents matcher patterns for tools, MCP tools, and wildcard hooks.
Lists security practices for path checks, command blocking, timeouts, and logging.
limitations: Does not install or enable hooks automatically.
Requires users to write and maintain their own hook scripts.
Shell examples assume jq and a Unix-like environment.
Audit logging examples must be adapted to avoid sensitive data exposure.

use_cases.title: Validate tool usage before execution
use_cases.description: Block writes outside a project or deny dangerous shell commands before Claude Code runs them.

use_cases.title: Create local audit trails
use_cases.description: Record selected hook metadata for compliance or debugging without storing sensitive tool input.

use_cases.title: Initialize project sessions
use_cases.description: Run setup checks or load safe project context when a Claude Code session starts.

prompt_templates.title: Explain hook basics
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the Claude Code hook events in this skill and recommend which event I should use for validating file writes.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a validation hook
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this skill, draft a PreToolUse hook that blocks writes outside CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR and explain how to add it to settings.json.

prompt_templates.title: Review a hook configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Claude Code hooks configuration for unsafe matchers, missing timeouts, and risky commands. Suggest safer alternatives.

prompt_templates.title: Design a secure audit workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a PostToolUse audit logging workflow that records useful metadata but redacts prompts, file contents, secrets, and command arguments.

output_examples.input: I need to block unsafe Bash commands before they run.
output_examples.output: Use a PreToolUse hook with matcher Bash. The response identifies dangerous command patterns, recommends quoted variables, and shows where to add a timeout.

output_examples.input: How should I log hook activity for debugging?
output_examples.output: Log only event type, tool name, timestamp, and a request identifier. Avoid storing prompts, file contents, environment values, or full command arguments.

output_examples.input: Which hook runs when Claude starts a project session?
output_examples.output: Use SessionStart for startup checks or safe context loading. Keep the script short, scoped to the project, and resilient to missing optional files.

best_practices: Use project-scoped paths and validate resolved paths before acting on hook input.
Add short timeouts to every hook so automation cannot stall Claude Code.
Redact or omit sensitive fields before writing any audit or debug logs.
anti_patterns: Do not log full hook input because it may contain secrets or private code.
Do not use wildcard matchers without understanding every tool they include.
Do not source broad environment files unless each variable is required.

faq.question: What are Claude Code hooks?
faq.answer: They are user-configured commands that run during Claude Code events, such as before tool use or after a tool completes.

faq.question: Can this skill install hooks for me?
faq.answer: No. It documents configuration patterns and examples. You must create scripts and edit settings yourself.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatibility, with content focused on Claude Code settings.

faq.question: Are hook scripts safe by default?
faq.answer: No. Hook scripts can run commands, read files, and write logs. Review each script before enabling it.

faq.question: What should I avoid logging?
faq.answer: Avoid logging prompts, file contents, command arguments, environment values, API keys, tokens, and full tool input JSON.

faq.question: What dependency do the examples use?
faq.answer: Many shell examples use jq to parse hook JSON input, so jq must be installed for those scripts.
